subject: Re: Private Observability Min Pack — audit logging + Grafana access controls
body:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@helioxbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Mehta <raj.mehta@helioxbank.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Private Observability Min Pack — audit logging + Grafana access controls

Hi Naomi,

As part of our security review for Redwood Private (VPC now, with on-prem as a future option), we need clarity on audit logging for the observability components you bundle.

Specifically:
1) Grafana: do you provide audit logs for (a) logins, (b) dashboard views/exports, and (c) changes to dashboards/data sources/alert rules?
2) Prometheus/Alerting: can we audit who changed alert rules / thresholds?
3) Minimum recommended controls: RBAC model, MFA requirements, and any baseline “least privilege” guidance.
4) What does Redwood consider “supported” for audit evidence (i.e., what we can show an auditor)?

If you have a short writeup, feel free to attach.

Thanks,
Laura
—
Laura Chen
Director, GRC
Heliox Bank



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@helioxbank.com>
Cc: Raj Mehta <raj.mehta@helioxbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private Observability Min Pack — audit logging + Grafana access controls

Hi Laura,

Thanks — this is a common set of questions for regulated Private deployments.

High level: the “minimum pack” is intentionally backend-agnostic, and we try to make the audit story work even in constrained (VPC / limited egress / air-gapped) environments. We don’t introduce a new proprietary audit backend; instead we recommend a set of standard audit sources depending on which components you run.

Short answers by area:

1) Grafana audit logging
- Authentication & MFA: we recommend running Grafana with SSO (SAML or OIDC) via your IdP, with MFA enforced at the IdP layer. In that setup, login/auth events are best sourced from IdP audit logs.
- “Who viewed which dashboard” / “who exported data”: Grafana’s native capabilities vary by edition and configuration. In most Private installs we see customers rely on a combination of:
  (a) IdP audit logs (authn/authz events)
  (b) reverse proxy / ingress access logs in front of Grafana (request-level access records)
  (c) Grafana server logs for admin/config events (limited)
  (d) optional: Grafana Enterprise audit logs, if your policy requires a first-class audit stream at the app layer.
- Changes to dashboards/data sources: for the min pack we strongly prefer GitOps/provisioning (dashboards and data sources provisioned from files/ConfigMaps), and we treat changes as code changes. Audit evidence then comes from (a) your SCM change history/approvals and (b) Kubernetes audit logs capturing changes to the underlying resources.

2) Prometheus / alerting rule changes
- The pack ships PrometheusRule resources (or rules files depending on your Prometheus operator). We recommend managing those via Helm/GitOps.
- Audit sources are:
  (a) SCM history + PR approvals (who changed thresholds)
  (b) Kubernetes audit logs for CRD changes (who applied/modified PrometheusRule)
  (c) CI logs for rule linting/validation (promtool), if you keep those as audit artifacts.

3) Recommended control mappings / baseline controls
- MFA: enforce via IdP for Grafana; for Kubernetes access enforce MFA where your identity layer supports it.
- RBAC: least privilege for (a) viewing dashboards, (b) editing dashboards, (c) managing alert rules, (d) managing data sources.
- Change control: dashboards + alert rules provisioned, and direct UI edits disabled (or limited to break-glass) where feasible.

4) What Redwood calls “supported” evidence
- We can document the standard log sources and the configuration knobs we support. In private environments, the customer typically owns (and can retain) the IdP logs, Kubernetes audit logs, ingress logs, and SCM history.

I’m attaching a short PDF we use internally that summarizes the above and provides specific configuration recommendations.

Attachment: Private_Observability_Min_Pack_Audit_Logging_Considerations_v0.3.pdf

If helpful, we can also walk through your evidence expectations (SOC 2 / ISO / internal policy) and map to the sources you already retain.

Best,
Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Product Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Raj Mehta <raj.mehta@helioxbank.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@helioxbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 4, 2025 at 8:46 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private Observability Min Pack — audit logging + Grafana access controls

Raj — replying inline.

A) Grafana OSS + ingress: evidence expectations
Yes, you can get to an “auditor-friendly” story without Grafana Enterprise, but it’s important to be explicit about what evidence comes from which system.

1) Dashboard + data source changes (strongest path)
- Recommended: manage dashboards and data sources via provisioning (files/ConfigMaps) and disable UI editing for most roles.
- Evidence sources:
  - SCM: commit history + PR approvals (who/what/when/why)
  - CD/GitOps: deployment history (which revision applied)
  - Kubernetes audit logs: records of changes to ConfigMaps/Secrets/PrometheusRule (who applied)

2) User access (“who accessed Grafana”)
- Preferred: IdP audit logs for authentication events.
- Supplementary: ingress/reverse-proxy access logs (timestamp, source IP, request path). This can show “user X established a session / accessed Grafana endpoints,” depending on how you propagate identity (e.g., OIDC) and what your proxy logs.

3) “Who viewed dashboard Y” / “who exported panel data”
- In Grafana OSS, there’s not always a clean, canonical audit event stream for every view/export action.
- Common approaches we see accepted by auditors:
  - policy + control: restrict who can access Grafana at all + enforce MFA at IdP + limit export permissions to a small admin group
  - technical: ingress logs + IdP logs + Grafana server logs (best-effort) + retention policy
- If your auditor requires explicit, per-action audit events (view/export) from the app, that’s the point where Grafana Enterprise audit logs (or an alternative dashboard tool with first-class audit logging) becomes the “cleanest” option.

B) Break-glass UI edits detection
We recommend not relying on ad-hoc UI edits, but if you allow them:
- Provisioned dashboards are typically overwritten/reconciled by provisioning on restart/reload; “drift” can be detected operationally by periodically re-applying provisioning and checking for diffs (GitOps tooling can help here).
- You can also restrict edit rights so only a break-glass group can modify dashboards; Kubernetes audit logs + SCM would show no corresponding change, which is itself an indicator of out-of-band modification.
- Practically: the most defensible path is (1) disable edits for standard roles, (2) require change tickets + time-bound access for the break-glass group, and (3) treat any UI edits as temporary, with a post-incident requirement to upstream the change into code.

Marcus and Kevin are cc’d because they own the secure-defaults/RBAC guidance and audit export integration patterns, respectively.

If you can share which framework(s) you’re aligning to (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FFIEC, etc.), we can map the above controls explicitly.

Best,
Naomi

Subject: Re: Private Observability Min Pack — audit logging + Grafana access controls

Laura/Raj — Marcus here (Security Eng lead). Adding a bit more detail on access controls for the “minimum pack” defaults.

Grafana access controls (recommended defaults)
- Authn: OIDC or SAML via your IdP; Grafana local users disabled except an initial bootstrap admin (rotated/disabled after setup).
- MFA: enforced in IdP.
- Session settings: short session TTL + idle timeout; secure cookies; TLS only.

RBAC model (typical)
- Viewer: read-only dashboards, no Explore, no data source access.
- Operator: can acknowledge/silence alerts (if using Grafana alerting), view dashboards, limited Explore.
- Admin (break-glass): manage dashboards/data sources; membership restricted and time-bound.

Network controls
- Put Grafana behind your ingress with IP allowlisting / private network access only.
- Separate admin access path if you need it (e.g., dedicated VPN segment).

Kubernetes / cluster-level controls
- All changes to PrometheusRule / ConfigMaps should go through GitOps/Helm.
- Enable Kubernetes API audit logging (most managed K8s support this; for on-prem we can provide recommended audit policy). This is the key audit source for “who changed the rule/dashboards at runtime.”

What we can support/document
- Recommended RBAC roles and sample config.
- Guidance on which logs to forward to your SIEM (IdP, ingress, Kubernetes audit logs, and optionally Grafana logs).

Happy to jump on a call if you want to align on your “break-glass” process.

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private Observability Min Pack — audit logging + Grafana access controls

Adding specifics on SIEM export since that often becomes the blocker in Private environments.

For audit-related logs, we typically recommend forwarding these sources to your SIEM (Splunk/QRadar/etc.):

1) IdP audit logs
- Authentication events for Grafana and for cluster access.

2) Ingress / reverse proxy logs
- Request logs for Grafana (and optionally Prometheus), including user identity fields if available.

3) Kubernetes audit logs
- API server audit: updates to ConfigMaps/Secrets, PrometheusRule CRDs, and any RBAC changes.
- For air-gapped/on-prem, this can be shipped via a node-level agent (Vector/Fluent Bit) to an internal SIEM endpoint.

4) Grafana server logs (optional)
- Useful for admin/config events and troubleshooting.

Supported forwarding targets (min pack defaults)
- HTTP(S) to a customer-managed endpoint (common)
- Syslog (TCP+TLS) where required
- Object storage (for batch export) in VPC environments

We’ll avoid shipping secrets; any headers/tokens should be configured as references (K8s secrets) and redaction rules can be enabled at the collector.

If you can confirm which SIEM and which transport you require, I can point you to a recommended collector config pattern.

—
Kevin Osei
Audit Log Export & SIEM Integration Engineering
Redwood Inference

Naomi/Marcus/Kevin,

Understood on Grafana OSS limitations for per-dashboard view/export auditing.

For our initial phase, we can proceed if:
- dashboards + data sources + alert rules are provisioned via GitOps (no routine UI edits)
- IdP MFA is enforced and we retain IdP audit logs
- we retain ingress logs + Kubernetes audit logs in Splunk
- break-glass access is time-bound and ticketed

Two remaining asks:
1) Please provide a short “control mapping” paragraph we can drop into our internal policy doc (ISO 27001 A.8/A.12 logging & monitoring + SOC 2 CC6/CC7 style language is fine).
2) Confirm that Redwood’s “supported” criteria for Private doesn’t require Grafana Enterprise.

If you can send those in email (no need for a formal doc), we’ll close this section.

Thanks,
Laura
